text: Track 3.1 So, we're going to look at some of the ways that technology has affected education and learning. Nowadays, thanks to technology, information is available to everyone. Most people have a computer, laptop or phone, so they only need to go online and they can find out information about almost anything. It is easy to forget how much more difficult it was in the past. Research took much longer because you had to be in the same place as your information. People spent hours in libraries finding the right books and then looking through them. Now, due to the internet, you don't even need to get out of bed to research your essay. But information is not the same as knowledge. We can go online and see a lot of facts, but that does not mean we understand them. And research shows that our memory can get worse due to computers. We become less able to remember details and facts. Since the light from computer screens makes our eyes tired, we also pay less attention when we read online. Research shows that many people understand a difficult new subject faster when they study it from books. And children have problems too. For example, in primary schools, many children's handwriting is bad because they use a mouse and keyboard more than they hold a pencil. Teenagers use technology and the internet for a large part of the day, which can affect their results at school, their social lives and even their health. Why should they go and meet friends in the park when they can just open an app on their phones and chat with their friends from their bedrooms? But technology has many more advantages than disadvantages, and it offers us many exciting new learning opportunities. For example, there are lots of websites that teach you any skill you want, often for free. You can learn languages, take dancing, cooking or art lessons, or watch videos explaining Einstein's theory of relativity. The most difficult thing is deciding where to start.
